intent: My last three keyboards each died inside two years, one from a stuck key, one from a flaky cable, one from letters wearing blank. This time I want to buy once and be done for a decade. Switches advertise 50 or 100 million keystroke ratings, but I have no idea whether that number means anything in real desks-and-coffee life, or whether it's actually the keycaps, stabilizers, or circuit board that give out first. Which boards do long-term owners say are still going strong after years of daily abuse, and what would you pick as the genuine buy-it-for-life option?

intent_v1_legacy: I've got $5,000 sitting in checking and I'm finally opening my first brokerage account, but I've been stuck for weeks between Fidelity, Schwab, Vanguard, Robinhood, Betterment, and the rest. My non-negotiables: no commissions on US stocks and ETFs, fractional shares since I can't afford whole shares of everything, tax-loss harvesting if possible, and an app that won't make me feel like I'm flying a plane. Can you actually compare the main platforms against those needs, factoring in what real users complain about, and just rank the ones you'd open first?

tri_source.angle: Buy-once-for-a-decade board: what fails first in practice (switch lifetime ratings vs keycaps, stabilizers, controller) and which boards survive
